coverage.headline: SEC sues Goliath Ventures over alleged $425M crypto Ponzi scheme
coverage.summary: The SEC alleges Goliath Ventures raised $425 million from roughly 1,300 investors and never made a single liquidity-pool investment, with the founder emailing false explanations to investors after payments halted in November 2025. The agency is seeking permanent injunctions, disgorgement with interest, and civil penalties.

coverage.headline: Goliath Ventures hit by SEC, CFTC in $425M crypto case
coverage.summary: The SEC and CFTC filed complaints on August 11 in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida, with the SEC alleging Goliath raised at least $425 million from over 1,300 investors and the CFTC citing approximately 1,600 customers and at least $397 million. Delgado's criminal sentencing was rescheduled to October 21, 2026, before U.S. District Judge Gregory A. Presnell in Orlando.

coverage.headline: CFTC accuses Goliath of $397M crypto Ponzi scheme as CEO awaits sentencing
coverage.summary: The CFTC's complaint alleges Goliath Ventures collected Bitcoin, Ether, and other cryptocurrencies from November 2022 through February 2026, with customer funds used for Ponzi payments rather than liquidity pools. The complaint further alleges Delgado's personal spending included $838,000 for a yacht, and that corporate card expenditures totaled $4.9 million in travel and $2.9 million in luxury goods.

coverage.headline: SEC, CFTC Sue Goliath Ventures Over Alleged $425M Crypto Ponzi Scheme
coverage.summary: Both the SEC and CFTC filed separate civil complaints on August 11 against Goliath Ventures and founder Christopher Delgado, with the SEC alleging an unregistered securities offering and the CFTC alleging commodity fraud. The two agencies' differing dollar figures—$425 million (SEC) and $397 million (CFTC)—reflect their distinct regulatory perspectives on the same alleged scheme.

coverage.headline: Goliath Ventures Faces SEC, CFTC Suits Over $400M Ponzi
coverage.summary: The SEC and CFTC filed parallel civil lawsuits against Goliath Ventures and founder Christopher Delgado, with the SEC alleging none of the investor funds or crypto assets were placed into the promised liquidity pools and that Delgado diverted at least $51 million for personal use. The CFTC is seeking restitution, disgorgement, civil penalties, trading and registration bans, and a permanent injunction.

coverage.headline: SEC, CFTC Sue Goliath Over $400M Crypto Ponzi Scheme
coverage.summary: The SEC and CFTC filed parallel civil complaints against bankrupt Goliath Ventures Inc. and founder Christopher Delgado, alleging they orchestrated a $400 million cryptocurrency Ponzi scheme. The SEC accused Goliath of raising at least $425 million from over 1,300 investors through fraudulent promises of returns from crypto liquidity pools.

coverage.headline: Crypto Firm, CEO Accused of Running $400 Million Ponzi Scheme
coverage.summary: The SEC and CFTC filed separate civil suits against Goliath Ventures Inc. and CEO Christopher Delgado, alleging they ran a roughly $400 million cryptocurrency Ponzi scheme in which investors were promised returns from crypto liquidity pools that never received any funds. Delgado had previously pleaded guilty to related criminal charges in June 2026.

coverage.headline: Goliath Ventures CEO pleads guilty in $400 million crypto Ponzi case
coverage.summary: Christopher Alexander Delgado pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, and money laundering, admitting to causing at least $250 million in losses and agreeing to forfeit luxury assets. The bankruptcy cases remain pending before Judge Robert A. Mark, with Delgado's sentencing set for October 8.

coverage.headline: Goliath Ventures CEO Pleads Guilty To Crypto Ponzi Scheme
coverage.summary: Former Goliath Ventures CEO Christopher Alexander Delgado pleaded guilty to wire fraud and money laundering charges tied to an alleged $400 million crypto Ponzi scheme. His sentencing hearing is scheduled for October 8, 2026.

coverage.headline: Florida Judge Appoints Receiver to Oversee Assets of Crypto Firm Goliath Ventures
coverage.summary: A Broward Circuit Court approved the motion to appoint Michael Budwick of Meland Budwick as receiver over collapsed cryptocurrency hedge fund Goliath Ventures. The receiver subsequently filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy petitions for both Goliath entities on March 16, 2026.
